reasons: The checks are short and clear.
No test is visible in the packet.
The docstring says a single number repeated three times is a common misuse, which the code does not detect.

terms.meaning: A plausible low to high span around an estimate, based on judgement rather than statistics.
The working assumption used as the central figure, which need not be the midpoint of the band.
A message raised when data breaks a rule, so it is not stored.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module purpose and rules
sections.what: Explains that estimates are ranges and that totals, currency and rolled-up figures must never be written into a range. Sums belong in the value package.
sections.why: The docstring keeps arithmetic in one place so it can be tested for reproducibility.
sections.watch_out: Adding a sum or cost figure to these ranges would bypass the value package's rules.

sections.name: Range
sections.title: Basic low, base and high estimate
sections.what: Holds three numbers for one quantity and checks that they are in order. The width property returns the gap between the high and low values.
sections.why: The docstring says the three values are a credible band that the value engine widens as confidence falls.
sections.watch_out: The docstring warns against repeating one number three times. The code allows it, so reviewers must catch it.

sections.name: NonNegativeRange
sections.title: Range that cannot go below zero
sections.what: A range where the lower bound must be zero or more, used for quantities such as effort or elapsed time.
sections.why: The docstring says a negative lower bound is a malformed estimate rather than a cautious one.
sections.watch_out: The rule only checks the lower bound, so the upper bound can still be any number.

sections.name: UnitRange
sections.title: Range limited to zero to one
sections.what: A range that must stay between zero and one, used for every share and rate in the schema.
sections.why: The docstring says a share above one is a category error, since no more than all of the work can be automated.
sections.watch_out: Values such as percentages written as whole numbers, like 40, will be rejected rather than converted.

summary: Defines a low, base and high estimate for one quantity, with optional limits that stop values going below zero or above one.
purpose: Lets agents give a credible range for estimates rather than a single number, which hides uncertainty.
why: The docstring says a point estimate hides the uncertainty the value engine needs to produce a downside case, and invites readers to treat a guess as a measured figure.
how: First, a range holds three numbers and checks that low is not above base and base is not above high. Second, the width property gives the gap between high and low. Third, a non-negative range rejects any negative lower bound. Fourth, a unit range rejects any bound outside zero to one, which is used for shares and rates.
inputs: Three numbers for low, base and high, for the non-negative and unit versions as well.
outputs: A frozen range object, plus its width. Invalid values raise a validation error.
risks: The range is only a holder. It does not check that the numbers are plausible. The docstring forbids storing totals or money in a range, and nothing in this file enforces that.
debug: If a range is rejected, check that the three values are in order. If a non-negative or unit range is rejected, check the lower bound and upper bound against zero and one.
